title: 教育原理（春期集中講義）
subtitle: Principles of Education
teachers:
IZAWA Shigeki
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: The goal of this course is to have one's own view of education through a fundamental study of education. To that end, based on educational theory, clarify the actual issues of school education, home education, and social education, and cultivate the basic ability to think about future education.
advice:
This course covers the items as below.

1. What is “Education”?
 The significance and goal of education, “Learning” and “Teaching”, The structure of school education, The significance of “Pedagogy”
2. Philosophy of Education and the history of school education
 Nature and education, The thought of new education movement, The method and Philosophy of education, The thought of national education
3. The history of school education
 The establishment of modern school, The issues of school education
4. Lifelong education
 The significance of lifelong education, Home education and social education
5. The issues of the current education
 Education in cooperation with community, The future education
books: Kyouiku to Manabi no Genri: Hendo suru Syakai to Mukiau tame ni, (The University of Nagoya Press.(The Principle of Education and Learning: For the moment of facing a changing society.)
requiredKnowledge: This course is for those who are serious about becoming a teacher.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Understand the principle of education and make the perspectives on education clear in consideration of issues of education.

(2) Understand the relationship between teaching and learning from the history of school education and think about education in terms of human life and lifelong learning.

(3) Suggest the solutions to the issues of current education from the social perspectives.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Understand the principle of education and make the perspectives on education clear.

(2) Understand the relationship between teaching and learning from the history of school education and think about education.

(3) Consider he issues of current education from the social perspectives.
